title: Assessing Functional Metrics of Skeletal Muscle Health in Human Skeletal Muscle Microtissues
protocol: Prepare ~ 110 g of PDMS polymer solution in a disposable plastic cup at a 1:15 ratio of monomer to curing agent using the components in the silicone elastomer kit.
Stir the polymer solution for 2-3 min using a 5 mL disposable serological pipette until completely mixed and homogenous.
Degas the mixture at room temperature by placing the cup within a benchtop vacuum chamber connected to a standard duty dry vacuum pump for ~30 min, or until all bubbles are removed.
Break the vacuum every 5-10 min to aid in degassing.
Use an empty 50 mL syringe barrel to plunge air and blow out any remaining bubbles on the surface of the polymer mixture as needed.
Remove leftover pieces of PDMS adhered to the PU negative mold by gently wiping down the edges and surface with a dry paper towel.

Spray the active surface of the PU negative mold with an even layer of release agent from top to bottom, then left to right while holding the can 15-20 cm away and using a fluid back and forth sweeping motion.
Rotate the mold 180° and repeat sprays.
Let the PU mold sit in the chemical hood for 10-15 min to dry.
Pour 100 g of PDMS evenly into the PU mold.
Place the mold within a vacuum chamber connected to a rotary vane vacuum pump.
Degas the PDMS-filled mold for approximately 45 minutes.
Break the vacuum seal every 5-10 minutes for the first 20 minutes to accelerate degassing.
Leave the mold in the vacuum chamber until all bubbles are removed from the PDMS mixture.
Transfer the degassed PDMS-filled PU mold to a 65 °C oven.
Incubate overnight to cure the liquid rubber.
Remove the cured PDMS positive plate from the oven.
Cool the plate at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.
With a bladeless scalpel, gently detach cured PDMS from the PU mold by running the back of the handle between the PDMS and walls of the mold.
Start along the upper edge and separate all 4 sides with the bladeless scalpel before pushing down to the base of the mold and detaching this portion.
Use both hands to push fingers underneath the plate, slowly peeling up and out of the PU mold.
Cut the plate into groups of 6 ± 2 MyoTACTIC wells using a single edge razor blade for tissue seeding purposes.
Place full MyoTACTIC plates or plate portions into an instrument sterilization bag.
Autoclave the bagged plates for a 25 min dry cycle at 120 °C and 100-140 kPag.
Thaw a vial of frozen cells in a 37°C water bath for less than 1 minute.
Transfer the contents of the vial to a 15 mL conical tube containing 9 mL of pre-warmed wash medium.
Centrifuge the 15 mL conical tube at 400 x g for 10 minutes.
Aspirate away the media carefully, avoiding the cell pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of growth media.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a 50 mL conical tube with 29 mL of growth media.
Transfer 10 mL of the media containing approximately 2.5 x 10^5 cells into a 100 mm x 20 mm cell culture dish.
Repeat the previous step with the remaining 20 mL of cell solution.
Place the cell culture dishes in a humidified cell culture incubator set to 37°C and 5% CO2.
Refresh the culture media every other day.
Culture the cells until they reach approximately 70%-80% confluency (typically 4-5 days).
Passage the cells as needed to achieve 1.5 x 10^5 cells for each hMMT generation.
Place a 6 well MyoTACTIC plate into a 10 cm cell culture dish 2-3 hours before cell seeding.
Add 100 μL of a 5% Pluronic F-127 solution to each well in the MyoTACTIC plate.
Seal the space between the 10 cm dish and lid with paraffin.
Centrifuge the 10 cm plate containing the MyoTACTIC portion at 1,550 x g for 1 minute to remove bubbles.
Store the 10 cm cell culture dish containing the MyoTACTIC plate at 4 °C until cells are prepared for seeding.
Slowly thaw one 50 µL basement membrane extract aliquot on ice within the culture hood.
Slowly thaw one 10 µL thrombin aliquot (100 U/mL stock solution) on ice within the culture hood.
Do not refreeze basement membrane extract aliquots after use.
Weigh approximately 7 mg of powdered fibrinogen in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Transfer the weighed fibrinogen to the cell culture hood.
Add 700 µL of 0.9% (wt/vol) NaCl solution to arrive at a 10 mg/mL final concentration solution.
Place the tube containing fibrinogen and saline in a 37 °C cell culture incubator for 3-5 min.
Remove and flick the tube gently.
Pulse spin the dissolved solution in a benchtop mini centrifuge.
Filter the fibrinogen solution using a 1 mL syringe outfitted with a 0.22 µm syringe filter.
Transfer the filtered fibrinogen solution to ice alongside the basement membrane extract and thrombin aliquots.
Pre-warm the hMMT seeding media at 37 °C before use.
Collect the cell culture plates from the culture incubator.
Aspirate the media from each plate.
Wash cells once with D-PBS by adding 5 mL of D-PBS into each culture plate.
Aspirate the D-PBS.
Detach the cells by adding 1 mL of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA into each culture dish.
Place the dishes in the cell culture incubator for 3 min.
Halt trypsin activity by adding 3 mL wash medium to the culture dish.
Transfer the cell solution to an appropriately sized conical tube.
Pellet the cells by centrifuging at 400 x g for 10 min.
Aspirate the media taking care to avoid the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of the wash medium.
Count cells using a hemocytometer and trypan blue dye under brightfield microscopy.
Dilute cell suspensions as needed before counting.
Resuspend 1,200,000 cells in 120 µL of ECM mixture to account for potential losses during preparation.
Transfer the cell suspension into a new conical tube.
Increase the volume to 10 mL with wash medium and spin at 400 x g for 10 min.
While cells are spinning down, prepare 150 µL ECM mixture in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube using DMEM, Fibrinogen solution, and Basement Membrane Extract.
Add 60 µL of DMEM to the ECM mixture.
Add 60 µL of Fibrinogen 10 mg/mL solution to the ECM mixture.
Add 30 µL of basement membrane extract to the ECM mixture.
Store the ECM mixture on ice until use.
Aspirate media from the conical tube containing the cell pellet.
Flick the end of the tube vigorously with a gloved finger to dislodge the pellet until it appears as a cell slurry.
Transfer 120 µL of ECM solution to the tube containing the cells.
Pipette up and down to thoroughly resuspend the cells within the ECM.
Place the cell-ECM solution on ice until use.
Retrieve MyoTACTIC plate portions containing Pluronic F-127 coated MyoTACTIC wells from a 4 °C refrigerator.
Aspirate the Pluronic F-127 solution from each well.
Allow residual Pluronic F-127 to release and settle at the bottom of the well for 5 min.
Aspirate again to remove any remaining Pluronic F-127.
Use a Pasteur pipette with a p1250 tip attached and a p200 tip over the p1250 tip when aspirating Pluronic F-127 solution.
Hover the pipette tip just over the oval pool while aspirating the Pluronic F-127 solution to avoid disrupting the coating.
Pipette carefully to resuspend any cells that may have sunk in the cell-ECM suspension.
Transfer 105 µL of cell-ECM suspension into a fresh, pre-chilled 1.5 mL tube.
Add 0.84 µL of thrombin stock solution to the 105 µL cell-ECM suspension to achieve a final concentration of 0.2 U/mg fibrinogen.
Pipette rapidly and carefully to mix thoroughly while avoiding introduction of bubbles.
Set p20 pipette to 15 µL before adding thrombin.
Use pre-chilled tips or dip the pipette tip into ice cold DMEM for a few seconds before collecting and transferring 15 µL of the cell-ECM mixture into each well.
Prepare cell-ECM mixture aliquots such that no more than 6 hMMTs are seeded at a time.
Add 15 µL of cell-ECM mixture (i.e., 150,000 cells) to each individual well.
Carefully add cell-ECM mixture to the center of the oval pool and avoid pressing the pipette tip into the bottom of the well.
With two light motions, spread the cell suspension behind each post in the well.
Once the surface is evenly coated in the cell-ECM suspension, move on to the next well.
Place the lid on the 10 cm culture plate containing the seeded wells.
Transfer the culture plate to a 37 °C tissue culture incubator for approximately 5 min.
Place the microcentrifuge tube with residual cell-ECM mixture into the incubator as a confirmation of gel polymerization.
After the cell-ECM mixture has polymerized, add 200 µL of prewarmed hMMT seeding media to each MyoTACTIC well.
Replace the lid on the 10 cm dish and return it to the incubator.
Remove the hMMT seeding media carefully using a pipette after 2 days of incubation.
Replace with 200 µL of prewarmed differentiation media containing 2% horse serum, 1% Pen/Strep, 4% ACA, and 10 µg/mL human recombinant insulin in DMEM.
Every other day thereafter, exchange half of the media with fresh differentiation media until day 12 of differentiation.
Set up a clear bottom glass or plastic stage mount on an inverted microscope.
Attach a smartphone camera to the microscope eyepiece using a microscope-camera mount.
Sterilize all surfaces and equipment with 70% ethanol.
Minimize traffic in the area during experimentation.
Cut approximately 30 cm of tin-coated copper wire.
Starting at the hub of a 25 G regular bevel needle, wrap about 10 cm of the wire tightly around the top half.
Leave about 20 cm of excess wire after wrapping.
Repeat for a second needle and then cut the hub off each needle.
Attach BNC to alligator clip connector cable to an output channel on the waveform generator.
Set the channel for square pulses with 20% duty cycle, 5 V amplitude (electrical field strength of 10 V/cm).
Alter frequency between 0.5 Hz and 20 Hz for twitch and tetanus contractions respectively.
Place a MyoTACTIC plate portion containing hMMTs on the microscope stage.
Gently insert each electrode bevel end into the PDMS directly behind each post in the oval pool.
Carefully tape down the 20 cm sections of excess wire to the microscope stage so that the needles remain vertical and ~10 cm of each wire remains free for connection.
Wear a thimble on the index finger to apply light pressure to the electrode during insertion into the PDMS.
Focus the microscope field of view on one post, ensuring focus is sharp on the post edge closest to the electrode.
Lock the smartphone camera focus to the clearest area of the post.
Connect the free ends of the taped wires to the waveform generator via alligator clamps.
Start video recording on the smartphone camera.
Turn on the channel output to initiate stimulation.
Induce hMMTs to undergo 3 twitch and 3 tetanus contractions, with a 2 min rest between the twitch and tetanus stimulation series.
Turn off channel output after stimulation.
Detach alligator clips from the tin-coated copper wires.
Remove the tape from the wires.
Wipe each electrode with 70% ethanol before inserting into subsequent hMMT wells.
Repeat procedure for all hMMTs.
Limit the time that hMMTs spend outside of incubator by stimulating no more than 3 tissues at a time.
Return the plate to the incubator for 10 min if additional hMMTs within the MyoTACTIC plate portion remain to be analyzed.
Select a region of interest (ROI) along the post edge to be tracked for post displacement using the custom script available on GitHub.
Press Enter to confirm the ROI and press Enter again to run the script.
Increase the ROI size in the code if the tracker fails during contraction due to large deflections, then adjust the script comments as necessary.
Enter y to confirm that the video contained multiple contractions when prompted by the script.
Enter y or n for exporting results to a .CSV file based on whether you wish to export the data.
Ensure post deflection results are reported as displacement in pixels for each contraction.
Convert pixels to µm values for the microscope 10x magnification setting.
Convert post displacement numbers to absolute contractile forces (µN) by multiplying values (µm) by the force-displacement conversion factor of 2.36 µN / µm.
Set up the microscope stage and stimulation equipment as previously described in step 4.
Launch microscope imaging software, select the FITC filter channel, and select movie recording function.
Set at an exposure of 500 ms and a resolution of 680 x 510 (Binning 2x2).
Ensure exposure is consistent for all hMMTs within an experiment.
Close the microscope shutter and keep the FITC channel off until ready to record calcium handling.
Retrieve the MyoTACTIC plate portion containing the hMMTs to be analyzed and set it directly on the microscope stage.
Insert and connect electrodes as previously described.
Focus the field of view on the center of the selected hMMT using brightfield.
Open the microscope FITC channel shutter, confirm blue light is on, and then select Movie Record in the software.
Turn on the output on the waveform generator to initiate electrical stimulation.
Induce the hMMT to undergo 8 twitch contractions.
Allow for 2 min of rest between the twitch and tetanus stimulation series.
Induce the hMMT to undergo 8 tetanus contractions.
Close the FITC shutter during the resting period.
Turn off the channel output.
Detach alligator clips from the tin-coated copper wires.
Remove the tape from the wires.
Wipe each electrode with 70% ethanol.
Insert electrodes into subsequent hMMT wells.
Stimulate and record procedure for all hMMTs.
Save movies in TIFF file format.
Open ImageJ for analysis.
Select Analyze, then Set Measurements.
Select Mean Grey Value and deselect other options.
Open a calcium (.tiff) video.
Outline the border of the microtissue using a polygon selection tool.
Save this area as the ROI.
Under More in the ROI Manager window, select Multi Measure.
Measure fluorescent intensity for all file slices at one row per slice.
Copy all measurements to a spreadsheet.
Compare the fluorescent intensity of each slice to the minimum spontaneous fluorescent intensity from the file using ΔF/F0 = (Fimmediate - Fminimum)/Fminimum.
Calculate the time for each frame by multiplying the movie recording frame speed by slice number.
Plot ΔF/F0 against time for the hMMT calcium transient response to stimulation.
Select the peak calcium transient signal for each of 6 consecutive contractions.
Average values to calculate the relative mean peak fluorescent intensity change of each hMMT.
Exclude data arising from the first twitch contraction from the overall analysis.
